opinions.rationale: Inverted-prior search for a mediated estimand, identification result, or software path under sustained strategies realized by cloning, artificial censoring and IPCW, or under sequential trial emulation, did not turn up a resolving paper or package. Highest-yield check was the report's own prior_work: Vansteelandt et al. 2019 (path-specific, randomly assigned treatment, planned mediator visits), Tai et al. 2023 (mediational g-formula with multiple time-varying mediators and R code), Vansteelandt and Daniel 2017 (interventional effects), Miles 2023 (interventional effects fail the sharp mediational null), Moreno-Betancur et al. 2021 (target trial of mediator interventions, not a treatment-strategy emulation under cloning), Domingo-Relloso et al. 2026 (path-specific plus competing risks for repeatedly measured mediators), Leigh et al. 2026 (protocol that prespecifies interventional mediation), and the applied TTE reports Eun et al. 2026 and Jang et al. 2026 (proportion mediated on hazard or subdistribution-hazard scales). Those works formalize or apply mediation for point, fixed longitudinal, or naturally time-varying exposure processes with planned or modeled mediator visits; none states an estimand or identification formula for a strategy population constructed by cloning and artificial censoring, nor for one person contributing to many sequential emulations. Broader 2024–2026 searches across AJE/Epidemiology/IJE/Stat Med/Biometrics-type venues, arXiv stat.ME, and medRxiv for combinations of mediation or path-specific or interventional indirect effects with cloning, clone-censor-weight, artificial censoring, sustained strategy, sequential trial emulation, or grace period returned applied TTEs that append mediation after a total effect, methods primers that list mediation and CCW as separate topics, and classic time-varying mediation (Lin et al. 2017 mediational g-formula for time-varying exposures; Zheng and van der Laan-type longitudinal mediation) that still assume an observed exposure process rather than an analysis-constructed strategy cohort. Package surface checks for TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, ltmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, and related tools did not surface a merged feature for mediated contrasts under CCW or sequential emulation. TARGET 2025 (Cashin et al., JAMA) still organizes reporting around the standard target-trial protocol components and does not add a required mediator, measurement-time, and intercurrent-event block. The closest adjacent proposal is Gonzalez-Perez, Wanis, Sarvet, and Stensrud (arXiv:2508.10702, 2025), which encodes separable effects for sustained treatments with identifying functionals and doubly robust estimators; that is a path-type decomposition of treatment components under sustained use, not classical mediation through a measured intermediate (for example HbA1c) when that intermediate also drives artificial censoring weights. Separable-effects theory therefore does not close the three nameable gaps in the statement: a mediated estimand for a sustained strategy under cloning or sequential emulation, identification when the mediator history enters the censoring weight, and a protocol component that fixes the mediator before analysis. Miles 2023 further keeps the natural-versus-interventional interpretability conflict open rather than solved. Queries run included: mediation + cloning/artificial censoring/CCW; interventional mediation + sustained strategy/IPCW; path-specific + grace period/clone-censor; sequential trial emulation + mediation; target trial + proportion mediated; arXiv/medRxiv sustained treatment + mediation/indirect/path-specific 2024–2026; TARGET guideline + mediator; CRAN/GitHub mediation hooks for the listed TTE and g-methods packages. Finding nothing that joins the pieces is itself the finding: the problem remains open as stated.
